_rubric: First tool call is scored. 2 = expected tool, schema-valid args, all expect_args matched. 1 = acceptable alternative tool with valid args, OR expected tool with valid args but an expect_args value mismatch. 0 = wrong tool, no call (when one is expected), hallucinated tool name, or schema-invalid args. For expected=null items, 2 = no tool call, 0 = any call.
system: You are a Linux performance investigation assistant. You can call tools to collect data. Call exactly one tool when data is needed; do not guess data. If no tool is needed, answer directly.

items.prompt: The service has rising p99 latency and CPU saturation. What should you inspect first?
Packets are being dropped on interface eth0 of the gateway host. Collect the relevant data.
Threads report long run-queue waits. Check the p99 time tasks wait to be scheduled.
Show me the last 50 error-level log lines from the payments service.
Run a 60-second CPU stress experiment in the lab to reproduce the contention.
Is CPU 7 experiencing scheduling delay?
Throughput dropped and we suspect TCP retransmissions. Gather network statistics for the last 5 minutes.
The checkout service is returning HTTP 500s. What has it logged recently?
Establish a 30 second baseline measurement in the lab before we inject any faults.
Load average is 40 on a 24-core host. Inspect its utilization.
Inject 120 seconds of network delay in the lab to test the client retry logic.
We suspect softirq time is high on host db-1. Check its CPU time breakdown.
We see RX ring buffer overflows on interface ens5. Get the NIC counters.
Collect warning-level logs from the auth service, at most 20 lines.
Tasks on CPU 3 seem starved. What is their median scheduling delay?
Reproduce memory pressure in the lab for 90 seconds.
Host web-2 is slow. Check its CPU over the last 10 minutes.
Are there TCP errors or drops on the network of host api-1?
The order service crashed. Get its info-level logs, 100 lines.
Check the p90 scheduler latency across all CPUs.
Requests on host storage-1 are stalling. Start by getting that host's CPU metrics.
Before diagnosing anything, check whether interface eth1 on host lb-1 has errors.
Deliberately run a 10 second CPU stress test in the lab so we can see how p99 reacts.
Look for timeout errors logged by the inventory service.
Context switches spiked. Check how long runnable tasks are waiting for a CPU.
What does p99 latency mean? Answer briefly; no investigation is needed.
Thanks, that's all for now.
Explain in one sentence what a cgroup is.
